faq: Do I own the design files?
Yes. We build the prototype in a design tool under an account you own or share it with you as editor, so you can hand it to any developer later. We do not keep copies behind a paywall.
Can the prototype be turned into a real product?
That is the point. Developers can read the screens and styles directly. We can build it from the same file, or you can hand it to another team. Either way nothing needs redrawing.
Where do the test users come from?
You supply them, for example friends in your target market, customers or a small waitlist. We write the script, run the sessions and report back. We do not buy fake testers or recruit through spam.
What if I only have a rough idea of the screens?
Send what you have, even hand drawn sketches or screenshots of apps you like. We ask a few questions, agree the screen list with you first, and only then start designing.

desc:
A clickable SaaS prototype and app design shows how your product will look and flow before any code is written. Ecom Swift LLC turns your feature list into linked screens in a design file you own, so you can test the idea with real people.

## What is a clickable prototype?

A clickable prototype is a set of designed screens linked together so that tapping a button moves to the next screen, just as it would in the finished product. Nothing runs behind it. There is no database or login logic, only the experience of using the product.

Designers build prototypes in dedicated design tools, and you open them through a shared link on a phone or laptop. People can try the flow, and you can watch where they hesitate.

## Why testing screens before code saves money

Changing a drawing is cheap. Changing finished software is not. If a prototype shows that users cannot find the main button or misunderstand the sign-up step, you fix it in an afternoon. The same discovery after development means rewriting code that has been paid for.

A prototype also ends arguments. When a founder, a partner and a developer each picture a different product, a set of screens gives everyone the same thing to point at and comment on.

## How a prototype improves decisions and the build

It brings feedback forward. Showing the flow to potential customers tells you whether the product makes sense to them before you commit to a build. Investors and early partners respond to something they can click far more readily than to a description.

For developers, a prototype is a clear specification. Screen layouts, button styles, form fields and error messages are already decided, so quotes are firmer and fewer questions arise during the build. Empty, loading and error states, often missed, are designed up front rather than invented under time pressure.

## What a good prototype includes

- The key screens of your main user flow, linked in order.
- Consistent buttons, form fields, spacing and headings.
- Your logo, colors and fonts where a branded version is chosen.
- Desktop and phone versions of the screens that matter most.
- Realistic sample content, not repeated placeholder text.
- Empty states, such as a dashboard with no data yet.
- Error and loading states for forms and lists.
- A small style guide that developers can follow.
- A shareable preview link that needs no sign-in.
- A short test script and notes on what testers found confusing.

## What we do

We start from your feature list or a scope document. We sketch the main flows on paper first, agree the order of screens with you, then design each screen and link them. You review a first pass, give comments and receive a revised version.

The Basic package delivers a handful of wireframe screens in one flow. Standard adds branding, more screens, a phone version and reusable components. Premium adds extra screens, a small style guide, the less visible states and a few test sessions with a written summary of where people struggled. Extra screens, logo work and animation are optional add-ons. The design file lives in a design tool account that you own.

## What to do, and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Start with the single most important user journey.
- Test with people who match your real customers.
- Watch where testers hesitate rather than asking if they like it.
- Keep screens consistent in spacing and wording.
- Save feedback in writing before changing anything.

**Avoid:**
- Designing every screen of a large product at once.
- Testing only with friends who want to be kind.
- Defending the design while someone is trying it.
- Polishing visual details before the flow works.
- Using random sample text that hides layout problems.

## Who this service is for

Founders with a feature list but no visual idea of the product benefit most. People pitching to investors or partners can show a convincing demo before development begins. Teams about to hire a developer can hand over screens instead of describing them in words.

## What we need from you

Your feature list or a short description of the main user journey, any logo or brand colors, and examples of products whose look you like. We create the design file in an account you own and invite you as editor. We never need passwords.
